summary: The lease-window repeat came back almost identical to the first run, which is the useful result here. Both cases verified at 0 ms with one of three voters reachable and the two non-voters answering, then lost leadership as the lease expired: the 500 ms lease failed at 507 ms after ten loop successes and the 1 s lease at 1015 ms after twenty, ending as Follower in both, against 510 ms and 1018 ms previously. The bound therefore reproduces to within ten milliseconds, so the account's reading that a false self-verification buys roughly one lease interval rather than a durable assurance is now supported by two runs rather than one. I added the receipt to the execution set beside the earlier lease and end-to-end receipts, appended the parsed results to the rationale and the repeat note to the joint history, and carried forward all six counterevidence items, the five limitations, both gap answers and the two knowledge uses at revisions 8 and 6. The conclusion stays explained with the scoped defect asserted.
